div.font: The universe is created from other natural processes, each distinct from the next.

div.font:
The universe is created from a collective effort of distinct gods, or the efforts of one
of them without the others.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 157px; height: 1px; padding-top: 275px; margin-left: 509px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 213px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.font:
"1 God, 3 Persons" defines a distinction
that is neither fundamental nor superficial (ie. neither consistent nor inconsistent, thus eliminating all valid possibilities), which is indistinguishable from a contradiction or false belief.
This requires us to infer that "inferring about reality doesn't reliably lead to spiritual truth", allowing the Trinity to be an exception to the rule. As such, the basis of verification shifts
from rational inference to textual authority, as

its truth now becomes entirely contingent upon proving that its scriptural source is perfectly preserved and divinely inspired. And, if truth is still distinguishable from falsehood, then the evidence must be superior against all other alternatives (which would all necessarily be false and pose some contradiction with reality).

div.font: The universe is created from one God, who is fundamentally distinct from all creation.

div.font:

Or, if the universe was created from nothing, then it didn't come "from" anything to begin with - which contradicts this inference.

not-universe, which could have been some multiversal structure.

div.span: However, this doesn't resolve the result of infinite regression, as now the question shifts to what caused the multiverse - without an observed answer.

font.span: Also, any explanation for the universe's origin is speculative, requiring us to infer that "arguments from ignorance are stronger than arguments of best-fit". However, this would also require the contradiction of "speculation is neither proof nor refutation" - ie. "speculation is proof/refutation".
